Rashi on Yevamot 23b:11:1.hebrew: היינו רישא - דהא אשמעינן ברישא, היו לו שנים, אחד חולץ ואחד מייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:11:1.english: This is the first clause - For [the Mishnah] already taught us in the first clause: [If] he had two [brothers], one performs chalitzah and one performs yibum.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:11:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא - הכא לא לייבם, כיון דחד מינייהו יש לו אח יחידי, לגזור תרי אחי דלא לייבם חד מינייהו אטו ההוא אח שאין לו אח שני, ואתי למפגע באחות זקוקה. קמ"ל:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:11:2.english: What might you have said - Here he should not perform yibum [levirate marriage]: since one of them has [only] a single brother, let us decree [regarding] two brothers that one of them should not perform yibum, on account of that brother who has no second brother and would come to stumble upon [the prohibition of] the sister of a zekukah [a woman bound by the levirate tie]. [Therefore, it] teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:12:1.hebrew: ודוקא מיחלץ - האח היחידי לשתיהן, והדר יבומי חד מהשנים אחר חליצת אחיו לשניה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:12:1.english: And specifically performing chalitzah - [by] the sole brother to both of them, and subsequently one of the two [brothers] performs yibum after his brother's chalitzah to the second [woman].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:12:2.hebrew: אבל יבומי ברישא - קודם חליצת היחיד לשתיהן, ואפילו חלץ אחיו של מייבם לאחותה, דליכא השתא איסור אחות זקוקה, לא [מייבם], משום שמא זו היא ארוסת הנכרי וקא פגע ביבמה לשוק בלא חליצה, דהיחידי הוא הנכרי ולו היבמה זקוקה. והא מילתא לא אשמעינן ברישא:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:12:2.english: But [to perform] yibum first - [that is,] prior to the single [brother's] chalitzah to both of them; and even if the brother of the one performing yibum performed chalitzah to her sister, so that there is now no prohibition of the sister of a zekukah [a woman bound to a levir], he may not [perform yibum], because perhaps this [woman] is the betrothed of the stranger, and he [thus] encounters [the prohibition of] a yevama to the public without chalitzah, for the single [brother] is the stranger, and to him the yevama is bound. And this matter was not taught to us in the first clause.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:13:1.hebrew: אחיו של זה מייבם חלוצתו של זה, הא תו למה לי - היינו הך, דהא אשמעינן ברישא: "השנים — אחד חולץ ואחד מייבם", וה"נ הכי הוא: דהני תרי — חד חליץ וחד מייבם, והני תרי — חד חליץ וחד מייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:13:1.english: The brother of this one takes the ḥalutza of that one in levirate marriage; why do I need this as well - This is identical [to that], for [the Mishnah] already taught us in the first clause: "[Where there are] two [brothers], one performs ḥalitza and one performs levirate marriage." And here too it is thus: of these two [brothers], one performs ḥalitza and one performs levirate marriage, and of those two [brothers], one performs ḥalitza and one performs levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:13:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא ניגזור דלמא - אתי ליבומי אחד משנים אלו ואחד משנים אלו בלא חליצה, וקפגע כל חד בספק יבמה לשוק ובאחות זקוקה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:13:2.english: Lest you say, let us issue a decree lest - one of these two and one of these two might come to perform levirate marriage without ḥalitza, and each one would encounter [the prohibition of] a doubtful yevama to an outsider and [that of] the sister of a woman bound [for levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:13:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - דלא גזרינן. והא מרישא לא שמעינן, דהתם לזה אחד ולזה שנים, דסוף סוף לא מייבם אלא חדא, וכיון דעוסקין בחליצה דחדא מדכרי נמי ולא מייבמי עד שיחלוץ היחיד לשתיהן. אבל הכא, כיון דלבסוף תרוייהו מייבמין — הך להאי ביתא והך להאי ביתא — אתי למימר: מה לנו ולחליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:13:3.english: This comes to teach us - that we do not issue [such] a decree. And we could not learn this from the first clause, for there, [the case is where] this one has one [brother] and that one has two, so ultimately only one [woman] is taken in levirate marriage, and since they are engaged in the ḥalitza of one, they will remember as well and will not perform levirate marriage until the single [brother] performs ḥalitza for both of them. But here, since in the end both of them perform levirate marriage — this one into this house and that one into that house — one might come to say: What need have we of ḥalitza?

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:14:1.hebrew: מאי שנא מהא וכו' ולא מתייבמות - וקתני סיפא: אם קדמו וכנסו, יוציאו; והכא קתני: אין מוציאין מידן:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:14:1.english: How is [this] different from that [mishna], etc., [and] they may not enter into levirate marriage - And the latter clause [of that mishna] teaches: If they went ahead and married [them], they must divorce [them]; whereas here [our mishna] teaches: we do not remove [them] from their possession.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:14:2.hebrew: חולצות ולא מתייבמות - ולא אמרינן: ליחלוץ חד מנייהו ודחי לזיקה דידה מאחיו, והאי מייבם חדא, כי מתני' דקתני מתייבמות שתיהן — כל אחת לאחר חליצת אחותה — כדקאמר: אחיו של זה מייבם חלוצתו של זה. לימא כולן חולצות כי התם! אמאי מהדרינן לייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:14:2.english: [They] perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage - And we do not say: let one of them perform ḥalitza [with one sister] and [thereby] remove her levirate bond from his brother, and [then] this [other brother] will perform levirate marriage with [the other] one, like our Mishnah, which teaches that both of them enter into levirate marriage — each one after the ḥalitza of her sister — as it states: "This one's brother performs levirate marriage with the ḥalutza of that one." Let us say [that here too] all of them perform ḥalitza, like there! Why do we strive to have [them] enter into levirate marriage?

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:15:1.hebrew: הכי השתא - התם זקוקות שתיהן להן. אי למ"ד בפרק ד' אחין טעמא דאין מתייבמת אפילו אחת מהן משום דיש זיקה, דמרישא מיתסרא משום דקפגע באחות זקוקה, וכי חליץ (מייבם) חד לחדא ופקע זיקה, לא משתריא אחותה לאידך, דכל יבמה שנאסרה שעה אחת על יבמה — אפילו לאחר נפילה — הרי היא כאשת אח שיש לה בנים ואסורה לעולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:15:1.english: How can [these cases] be compared - There, both [sisters] are bound [by a levirate bond] to them [the two surviving brothers]. If [it is] according to the one who says in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim [that] the reason even one of them may not enter into levirate marriage is because there is a levirate bond — for from the outset she is forbidden because he encounters the sister of a woman bound [to him] by a levirate bond, and when one [brother] performs chalitzah (variant: levirate marriage) with one [sister] and the levirate bond is severed, her sister does not become permitted to the other [brother], for any yevamah who was forbidden for [even] one moment to her levir — even after falling [before him for levirate marriage] — is like the wife of a brother who has children, and is forbidden forever.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:1:1.hebrew: ואין יודע אי זה מהן קידש - אסור בשתיהן, דכל חדא וחדא איכא למימר זו אחות אשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:1:1.english: And he does not know which of them he betrothed - He is forbidden to both of them, for [with regard to] each one it can be said [that] this [one] is [his] wife's sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:1:2.hebrew: חולץ לשתיהן - דלא ידע איזו היא יבמתו. ומיחלץ חדא וייבומי חדא לא, דאחות חלוצתו אסורה לו מדרבנן בחייה. ויבומי ברישא נמי לא, דדלמא לא זו היא יבמתו, וקפגע באחות זקוקתו דהויא כאשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:1:2.english: He performs ḥalitza with both of them - Because he does not know which one is his yevama. And performing ḥalitza with one and levirate marriage with [the other] one [is] not [permitted], because the sister of his ḥalutza is forbidden to him by rabbinic decree during her lifetime. And performing levirate marriage first [is] also not [permitted], lest this one is not his yevama and he encounters the sister of his zekuka [the woman bound to him for levirate marriage], who is like his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:2:1.hebrew: היו לו שנים אחד חולץ - תחלה לאחת, והשני, אם רצה לייבם לשניה, מייבם. דאם זו יבמתו, שפיר; ואם אחותה היא, לא קפגע באחות זקוקתו, דחליצה אפקעה לזיקה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:2:1.english: If he had two [brothers], one performs ḥalitza - first with one [of them], and the second [brother], if he wishes to take the second [sister] in levirate marriage, takes [her] in levirate marriage. For if this [second one] is his yevamah, [it is] well; and if she is her sister, he does not encounter the sister of a woman bound to him [by a levirate bond], since the ḥalitza removed the levirate bond.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:2:2.english: They went ahead and married [them] - Before they consulted the court.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:2:3.hebrew: אין מוציאין מידם - דכל חד וחד אמר: אנא שפיר נסיבי. ואי נמי הוה איפכא, שהראשון ליבום כנס אחות זקוקתו, ההיא שעתא ודאי הויא אסירא, ומשבא אחיו וייבם השניה שהיא יבמתו, פקע זיקה מאידך למפרע:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:2:3.english: We do not remove [them] from their possession - For each and every one [of them] says, "I married properly." And even if it was the reverse, that the first [brother] to perform levirate marriage married the sister of his *zekukah* [the woman bound to him by a levirate bond], [at] that moment she was certainly forbidden [to him]; and once his brother came and performed levirate marriage with the second [sister], who is his *yevamah*, the levirate bond was retroactively removed from the other [sister].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:3:1.hebrew: שנים שקדשו ב' אחיות - והם נכרים:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:3:1.english: Two [men] who betrothed two sisters - And they are unrelated [to each other].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:3:2.hebrew: זה חולץ לשתיהן וכו' - דכל חד וחד מינייהו אסור ליבומי, דדלמא באחות זקוקתו פגע:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:3:2.english: This [brother] performs ḥalitza with both of them, etc. - For each and every one of them is forbidden to perform levirate marriage, lest he encounter the sister of his zekukah [the woman bound to him for levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:4:1.hebrew: היחיד חולץ לשתיהן - כדפרישית לעיל, שאי אפשר לו לייבם — לא קודם חליצה משום אחות זקוקתו, ולא לאחר חליצה משום אחות חלוצה. לפיכך, הואיל ואסור לייבם, יחלוץ תחלה לשתיהם כדי להוציא אותה שהיא יבמתו מאיסור יבמה לשוק:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:4:1.english: The single [brother] performs ḥalitza with both of them - As I explained above, he cannot perform levirate marriage — neither before ḥalitza, because of [the prohibition against marrying] the sister of his zekukah [the woman bound to him for levirate marriage], nor after ḥalitza, because of [the prohibition against marrying] the sister of his ḥalutza. Therefore, since he is forbidden to perform levirate marriage, he must perform ḥalitza first with both of them in order to release the one who is his yevamah from the prohibition of a yevamah [marrying] into the general public.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:4:2.hebrew: והשנים אחד חולץ - לאפקועי זיקה מאחיו, אם זו היא יבמתו, ותשתרי אחותה לשני ממה נפשך. אם יבמתו היא, שפיר, ואם אחותה היא, הא קפקעה זיקת היבמה מיניה בחליצת אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:4:2.english: And [of] the two, one performs ḥalitza - To remove the levirate bond from his brother, if this [woman] is his yevamah, so that her sister will be permitted to the second [brother] either way: if she is his yevamah, well and good; and if she is her sister, the levirate bond of the yevamah has been removed from him through his brother's ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:4:3.hebrew: אחיו של זה מייבם חלוצתו של זה - ממה נפשך: אם זו יבמתו, שפיר נסיב, שהרי אחיו לא חלץ לזו, אלא לאחותה שלא היתה יבמתו, ואינה כלום. ואי לאו יבמתו, שפיר נסיב נכרית: דאי משום אחות זקוקתו, ליכא, שהרי חלץ אחיו לאחותה שהיא יבמתו ופקע זיקה; ואי משום יבמה לשוק, הרי חלצה זו מן היחיד שהוא אח בעלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:4:3.english: The brother of this one may take the ḥalutzah of that one in levirate marriage - Either way: if this [woman] is his yevamah, he marries [her] properly, for his brother did not perform ḥalitzah with this one, but rather with her sister, who was not his yevamah, and [that ḥalitzah] is nothing. And if [she is] not his yevamah, he properly marries an unrelated woman: for if [you object] on account of [her being] the sister of his zekukah [the woman bound to him by levirate attachment], there is no [prohibition], since his brother performed ḥalitzah with her sister, who is his yevamah, and the levirate bond has been severed; and if [you object] on account of a yevamah [marrying] an outsider, behold, this [woman] performed ḥalitzah with the one [brother] who is her husband's brother.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:5:1.hebrew: קדמו שנים - אחין של אחד וחלצו לשתיהן, משום דלא ידעי אי זו היא יבמתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:5:1.english: Two went ahead - [Two] brothers of one [of the deceased], and performed ḥalitza with both of them, because they do not know which one is his yevamah.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:5:2.hebrew: לא ייבמו השנים - אחים האחרים, זה את זו וזה את זו, דקמא דנסיב איכא למימר: זו היא אחות זקוקתו. אלא אחד חולץ תחלה לאחת ואחד מייבם לשניה, ממ"נ: אם יבמתו היא — שפיר; ואי לאו יבמתו היא — באחות זקוקתו לא פגע, שהרי חלץ אחיו ליבמתו, ויבמה לשוק נמי ליכא, שהרי היא חלוצה מאחי בעלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:5:2.english: The two may not perform levirate marriage - [Meaning] the other brothers, this one [marrying] this [sister] and that one [marrying] that [sister], for [regarding] the first one who marries, it can be said: "This one is the sister of the woman bound to him [by a levirate bond]." Rather, one performs ḥalitza first with one [sister] and one performs levirate marriage with the second, either way: if she is his yevamah, [it is] well and good; and if she is not his yevamah, he does not encounter [the prohibition of] the sister of the woman bound to him, since his brother has performed ḥalitza with his yevamah, and there is also no [prohibition of] a yevamah [marrying] an outsider, since she has received ḥalitza from her husband's brother.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:5:3.hebrew: ואם קדמו - אלו שנים האחרונים וכנסו אחר חליצת השנים הראשונים, ולא באו לימלך לב"ד — אין מוציאין מידם, כדפרישית, שאין כאן אלא ספק איסור אחות זקוקה בנשואין הראשונים. דאיכא למימר קמא דנסיב — יבמתו היא, ושפיר נסיב, ובתרא נמי שפיר נסיב נכרית. ואי נמי הוה איפכא, דקמא פגע באחות זקוקתו — כיון שבא שני ויבמה, פקע זיקתה מאחיו והותרה לו אשתו, ואיסורא דעבד עבד:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:5:3.english: And if they went ahead - [If] these latter two [brothers] went ahead and married [them] after the ḥalitza of the first two [brothers], and did not come to consult the court, we do not remove [their wives] from them, as I explained — for there is here only a doubt regarding the prohibition of the sister of a zekukah [a woman bound by a levirate tie] at the first marriage. For one can say [that the woman whom] the first [brother] married is his yevamah, and he married properly, and the latter [brother] also properly married an unrelated woman. And even if it was the opposite, that the first encountered the sister of his zekukah, once the second [brother] came and performed yibbum with her, her levirate bond ceased from his brother and his wife became permitted to him; and the prohibition that he committed, he committed.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:6:1.hebrew: שמעת מינה קדושין שאין מסורים לביאה - שאין סופן לבא לידי ביאה. דקס"ד דמתניתין בשלא הוכרו בשעת קדושין, לא הוה ידע הי מינייהו, כגון דאמר: "הרי אחת מכם מקודשת לי", ועשו שתיהן שליח לקבל קדושין. וקדושין אלו אין סופן לביאה, דכל חדא קיימא עליה בספק אחות אשה. ומדקתני: "נותן גט לזו וגט לזו", מכלל דחדא מיהא מקודשת, ומשום ספיקא דלא ידע הי מינייהו בעי למיתב גט לתרווייהו — אלמא קדושין הן. ופלוגתא דאביי ורבא היא בקדושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:6:1.english: You learn from this: betrothals that cannot lead to consummation - [That is,] whose end cannot come to consummation. For we initially assumed that our Mishnah [speaks of a case] where they were not distinguished at the time of betrothal — he did not know which of them [it was] — such as where he said, "Behold, one of you is betrothed to me," and both of them appointed an agent to accept betrothal. And these betrothals cannot ultimately lead to consummation, for each one stands before him under the doubt of [being his] wife's sister. And since [the Mishnah] teaches, "he gives a bill of divorce to this one and a bill of divorce to this one," it follows by implication that at least one [of them] is betrothed, and because of the doubt that he does not know which of them [it is], he must give a bill of divorce to both of them — thus, they are [valid] betrothals. And it is a dispute between Abaye and Rava in [tractate] Kiddushin.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:7:1.hebrew: שהוכרו - בשעת קדושין, ויודע היה את מי מקדש. הלכך, מסורים לביאה נינהו וחלו קדושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:7:1.english: That they were recognized - At the time of betrothal, and he knew whom he was betrothing. Therefore, [the betrothal] is given over to intercourse, and the betrothal took effect.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:7:2.english: And he does not know - [This] implies [that] now he does not know. "[It] is unknown" implies [that] the matter was never known.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:8:1.hebrew: ומאי קמ"ל - מתניתין? פשיטא דתרווייהו בעי גיטא, דלא ידע הי מינייהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:8:1.english: And what does it teach us - [i.e.,] the Mishnah? It is obvious that both of them require a bill of divorce, since he does not know which one of them [he betrothed].

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:8:2.hebrew: סיפא איצטריכא ליה - דקתני אחד חולץ ואחד מייבם, וקא שמעינן דוקא מיחלץ חד והדר יבומי אידך, ממה נפשך, כדפרישית לעיל:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:8:2.english: It was necessary [to teach] the last clause - which teaches [that] one performs ḥalitza and one enters into levirate marriage, and we learn [from this that] specifically one [must] perform ḥalitza [first] and then the other enters into levirate marriage, either way, as I explained above.

Rashi on Yevamot 23b:8:3.hebrew: אבל יבומי - חד ברישא, והדר מיחלץ שני לאידך — לא, דקמא דייבם, דלמא פגע באחות זקוקתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 23b:8:3.english: But [performing] levirate marriage - [for] one [brother to do so] first, and then the second [brother] to perform ḥalitza with the other [woman] — no, because the first [brother], who performs levirate marriage, perhaps encounters the sister of a woman bound to him [by a levirate bond].

Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:14:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא מהא דתנן - פי' בקונט' דפריך אהא דקתני במתני': "קדמו וכנסו אין מוציאין מידם". וקשה, דלפי זה ה"ל לאתויי סיפא דמתניתין דד' אחין; ועוד, דבסמוך מייתי סיפא דמתני' אברייתא דשילא. ואר"י דפריך אהא דקתני במתניתין: "אחד חולץ וא' מייבם", וגבי ד' אחין — שתיהן חולצות:
Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:14:1.english: And in what way is [this case] different from that which we learned - Rashi explained that [the Gemara] is raising an objection against that which is taught in the Mishnah: "If they went ahead and married [them], we do not remove [them] from their hands." And this is difficult, for according to this, [the Gemara] should have cited the latter clause of the Mishnah of Four Brothers; and furthermore, shortly below [the Gemara] cites the latter clause of the Mishnah against the baraita of Shila. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that [the Gemara] is raising an objection against that which is taught in our Mishnah: "One performs ḥalitzah and one performs levirate marriage," whereas regarding [the case of] Four Brothers — both [sisters] perform ḥalitzah:

Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:2:1.hebrew: קדמו וכנסו אין מוציאין מידם - אר"י: דווקא משום דשמא לא פגע באחות זקוקתו, אבל אי ודאי הוה זקוק להוציא. אף על גב דגבי שומרת יבם שקידש אחיו את אחותה (לקמן יבמות דף מא.) אין צריך לרבנן אפילו להמתין — היינו משום שקדש תחלה ולא בא עליה באיסור, דכבר נפטרה היבמה זיקתה ממנו בקדושי אחותה; אבל הכא דקני לה בביאה, דוקא במקום ספק הוא דאמרינן: "קדמו וכנסו אין מוציאין מידם", אבל בודאי לא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:2:1.english: If they went ahead and married, we do not remove [them] from their hands - Rabbi Yitzchak said: [This applies] specifically because perhaps he did not encounter the sister of his zekukah [the woman bound to him by levirate marriage], but if it were certain, he would be obligated to divorce [her]. Even though regarding a shomeret yavam [a woman awaiting levirate marriage] whose sister his brother betrothed (later in Yevamot 41a), according to the Rabbis he does not even need to wait — that is because he betrothed [her] first and did not cohabit with her in [a state of] prohibition, for the yevamah's levirate bond with him had already been released through the betrothal of her sister; however, here, where he acquires her through intercourse, it is specifically in a case of doubt that we say, "If they went ahead and married, we do not remove [them] from their hands," but in a case of certainty, no:

Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:6:1.hebrew: קדושין שאין מסורים לביאה - פירוש: דע"י קדושין קא מפסדה בביאה, אבל חייבי לאוין ועשה חשיבי קדושין המסורים לביאה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:6:1.english: Betrothals that are not given over to consummation - Explanation: [this means] that through the betrothal, consummation is forfeited, whereas [women forbidden by] negative commandments and a positive commandment are considered betrothals that are given over to consummation.

Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:7:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי דקתני אינו יודע - וא"ת: א"כ תקשה לאביי, דאמר בפ' האיש מקדש (קדושין דף נא. ושם) דהוי קדושין? וי"ל: דאין יודע משמע הכי ומשמע הכי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 23b:7:1.english: [It] is also precise, as it teaches: "He does not know" - And if you ask: If so, [this] poses a difficulty for Abaye, who said in the chapter [entitled] Ha'ish Mekadesh (Kiddushin 51a and there) that it is [a valid] betrothal? And one can answer that "he does not know" implies this and implies that [i.e., it can bear either interpretation].
